answer: In an agent economy that manages a meadow and its irrigation terrace, the payment kernel requires each worker identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding, with one active job allowed per bond. Creating 1,000 fake workers therefore ties up $100,000 for a month. Splitting into aliases grants no extra work capacity per dollar, so an attacker must fund every additional slot and bear the cost of immobilized capital.
